clue.text: Product from tree — a lot of matches

definitions.meaning: latex tapped from a tree is processed into this elastic material
in bridge, tennis or cricket a series of games or matches is called by this name

explanation.surface: A tree yields a product, and someone gripes about a huge lot of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural latex comes from a tree, and a series of matches in bridge or cricket is a rubber.

clue.text: Destroy Bible in fit of temper

indicators.note: the Bible abbreviation sits inside the word for a fit of temper

parts.note: a fit of temper is rage
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone tears up a Bible in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: AV, the Authorised Version, is a standard crossword shorthand for the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravage is to lay waste or wreck, a synonym of destroy.

clue.text: Singer swallows his first sedative

indicators.note: the singer takes a letter into his own middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a baritone is a male singer
his refers back to the singer, so his first letter is the opening B of baritone

explanation.surface: A singer gulps down his first dose of a sedative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his first' is not the first letter of 'his': it is the singer's own first letter, B, which the baritone then swallows.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbitone is a barbiturate drug formerly prescribed as a sleeping pill.

clue.text: Be right to leave son inside

indicators.note: the letter for son is placed within the word for a way out

parts.note: an exit is the right or means of going out
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son is granted the right to leave home.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being.

clue.text: Anger in excited press shows signs of life

indicators.note: the word for anger goes inside the shuffled letters
excited letters are stirred up, so the word press is rearranged

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: An angry, worked-up press is still very much alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges the five letters of the press word, and 'in' sets the anger word between the fourth and fifth of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that respires is breathing, the plainest evidence of being alive.

clue.text: Soothed, having stopped to get rid of head cold

indicators.note: the letter is dropped from the word for stopped

parts.note: ceased means having stopped

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A head cold eased once the sniffles stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' picks C from cold, and 'to get rid of' removes it from CEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means relieved or calmed, the same as soothed.

clue.text: In European cellar, try to reach bar with support

definitions.text: try to reach bar with support

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European
a vault is an underground cellar

explanation.surface: Down in a European cellar, someone strains to reach a bar using a prop.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bar' looks like a drinks bar near the cellar; it is the crossbar an athlete clears.
explanation.definitionFit: In this athletics event a jumper uses a long flexible stick to clear a high crossbar.

clue.text: Type asked to lend an ear

definitions.meaning: an upright typeface, as opposed to italic
Mark Antony begins his speech in Julius Caesar asking these citizens to lend him their ears

explanation.surface: A sort of person is asked to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright print is called roman type, and Shakespeare's Antony addresses Rome's citizens: 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'.

clue.text: Various things sulphur makes wet?

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
to undo drying is jokingly to un-dry, so un-dries means makes wet

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether sulphur dampens various items.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word UNDRIES, read as the opposite of dries.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items, various bits and pieces.

clue.text: Funny business, working with member of family

parts.note: a machine that is going is working
a son is a member of a family

explanation.surface: Some odd dealings are going on in a family firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are suspicious or improper activities, shady dealings.

clue.text: I'm nervous about being an unwilling host

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A host confesses anxiety about entertaining guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of I'M NERVOUS. The 'host' is not a party giver but a body carrying parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: Verminous means infested with lice or fleas, an involuntary host to pests.

clue.text: Fruit in mass consumed by Spanish city

indicators.note: the city eats the mass letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: León is a city in northern Spain
m is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Fruit in quantity is eaten up by a city in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a sour yellow citrus fruit.

clue.text: To shine, it's good to pay attention

parts.note: to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone advises that to shine, a good listener does well.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle or gleam with reflected light.

clue.text: One seeking water for two or three couples in restaurant

indicators.note: the numeral sits inside the word for a restaurant

parts.note: a diner is a cheap restaurant
three couples make six, VI in Roman numerals; two couples, IV, inserted one place earlier gives the same result

explanation.surface: A dowser goes looking for water on behalf of a few couples dining out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or' is fair: four (two couples) or six (three couples) in Roman numerals, placed one letter apart in the restaurant word, give the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A water diviner is a dowser who searches for underground water with a rod.

clue.text: Result of speculation there's some sign of ocean starting to boil?

definitions.meaning: the disastrous 1720 British share-dealing collapse caused by wild speculation

definitions.text: some sign of ocean starting to boil?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a bubble rising in southern waters, as when water begins to boil

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a spot of froth means the sea is about to boil.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1720 financial crash followed frenzied speculation in South Sea Company shares; literally, a bubble in a southern sea.

clue.text: Rowdy sort of boy once put up with childish toy

parts.note: a Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, often seen as a hooligan
to bear is to tolerate

explanation.surface: An old-time tearaway puts up with a child's plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in drape jackets, with a rowdy reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a soft stuffed toy for children.

clue.text: Desire to see a doctor — I can keep nothing in

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: the can holds the nothing letter inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A patient wants to see a doctor but cannot keep anything down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambition is a strong desire to achieve something.

clue.text: Stop working and rest on something soft

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a break is a rest
down is soft fluffy feathers

explanation.surface: Someone stops work for a rest on a soft cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: When a machine breaks down it ceases to function.

clue.text: Strong drink, but I shan't be drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling, so I shan't be is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone vows not to get tipsy on a powerful spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the letters of I SHAN'T BE; 'but' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a potent anise-flavoured spirit made with wormwood.

clue.text: Source of income often handed to one on a plate

definitions.meaning: the basic, regular work that pays the bills

definitions.text: often handed to one on a plate
definitions.meaning: slices of buttered bread are commonly served on a plate

explanation.surface: Someone's livelihood seems simply given to them on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and butter means one's staple livelihood, and literally it is buttered bread served at table.

clue.text: Sell control, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for control is spoken, matching another spelling

parts.note: a pedal is a foot control on a car or bicycle

explanation.surface: A salesperson is told to sell control.
explanation.walkthrough: A PEDAL, a foot control, is pronounced like PEDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle is to sell goods, typically by going from place to place.

clue.text: Expression of shock as interrogator clarifies his role?

definitions.meaning: a questioner explaining what he does would say he puts questions

explanation.surface: An interrogator, explaining his job, makes a shocked exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exasperated exclamation, and literally what someone asking questions does.

clue.text: One of the things that's on the cards undisguised in blunt speech

definitions.text: One of the things that's on the cards
definitions.meaning: one of the four card suits, alongside hearts, diamonds and clubs
plain speakers call a thing by its proper name, calling a garden tool by its own name

explanation.surface: Something likely to happen is stated plainly and bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the cards' means likely, but here it is a suit; 'call a spade a spade' means speak bluntly.
explanation.definitionFit: The suit symbol appears on playing cards, and the idiom about calling this tool by its name means speaking frankly.

clue.text: Leading group's surprising defeat

parts.note: up means ahead or leading, as in two goals up
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A team at the top suffers an unexpected loss.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is an unexpected win by an underdog, a shock defeat for the favourite.

clue.text: Mollusc stuck to stern of boat in a flash

indicators.note: the mollusc is attached directly beside the other piece
the stern is the rear of a boat, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: a winkle is a small edible sea snail

explanation.surface: A shellfish clings to the back of a boat for an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: In the twinkle of an eye means instantly, so twinkle is a moment.

clue.text: French composer drops Viennese one almost in it

indicators.note: the shortened composer is dropped inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Alban Berg was a composer born in Vienna

explanation.surface: A French composer abandons a Viennese colleague who has almost fitted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' means another composer: Alban Berg, of Vienna. 'almost' cuts him to BER, and 'drops ... in' puts that in IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Ibert was a 20th-century French composer.

clue.text: Meals with last of spare rib

parts.note: teas are light afternoon or evening meals

indicators.note: the final letter of the word spare is taken

explanation.surface: Meals served with the end of a spare rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rib' looks like part of a spare rib, but it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to mock them playfully.

clue.text: In rebuke, sound wholly lacking in warmth

indicators.note: the sound word is placed inside the word for a rebuke

parts.note: to scold is to rebuke
a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: A rebuke's tone is completely icy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-cold means completely cold, with no warmth at all.

clue.text: Hate to put value on senior manager

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other

parts.note: exec is short for executive, a senior manager
to rate is to put a value on something

explanation.surface: Someone hates having to appraise a senior boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to loathe or curse, a strong form of detest.

clue.text: Point of view taken in this, for example

indicators.note: the word in is removed from the longer word

parts.note: this clue serves as an instance, an example

explanation.surface: Someone states their view in this case, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this, for example' is an INSTANCE; take away IN and STANCE remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or attitude on an issue.
